object.title: Purpose and nature of the game

paragraphs.text: Moi Président is a satirical simulation game: a humorous and parodic work of fiction, loosely inspired by political news. The opponents, the parties, the events and the dialogues are fictional, and the names of the opponents and the parties are deliberately twisted.
The game’s polls, scores and results come from a simulation. They have no predictive value and measure nobody’s opinion. The game gives no voting instruction.
The game is not affiliated with any governmental organisation, political party or activist association, and is neither endorsed nor funded by any of them.
The game is free and is used without an account.
Its minimum age is that of the app stores’ ratings: PEGI 7 on Google Play and 13+ on the App Store. These ratings may vary from country to country.

The publisher grants you a personal, non-exclusive and non-transferable licence to use the game, on your devices, for non-commercial use. This licence does not allow you to copy, decompile or redistribute the game, subject to the rights the law grants you and to the licences of the third-party components and of the campaign kit.

Do not use the game or its screenshots to mislead about reality: do not present them as a real poll, a real result or a real statement by a candidate. Do not present the game as an official service or as electoral propaganda.
Use contrary to these rules ends your right to use the game. It does not trigger any fixed sum to pay. The publisher keeps the remedies the law gives it in case of harm.
The game, its texts, its illustrations and its logo are protected. Third-party fonts, icons and libraries are used under their licences, listed in “Credits and licences”.

Anyone named, referred to or parodied in the game may ask for a content to be corrected or removed by writing to support@gocosmic.dev. The publisher examines each request and, if it grants it, publishes the correction in an update of the game.
The campaign kit is optional. It is downloaded only at your request, from GitHub, a service of GitHub, Inc.
The game’s links to its sources open third-party sites in your browser. These sites have their own terms and their own privacy policy.
The privacy policy describes what the game does with your data: it stays on your device. Your acceptance of these terms is stored on your device only.

The game is provided free of charge, for entertainment. The publisher strives to correct it, without being able to guarantee that it is free of errors, that it works without interruption or that it remains available in the app stores.
The publisher is not liable for the consequences of using the game against article 4, nor for the content of the third-party sites the game links to.

Nothing in these terms excludes or limits the publisher’s liability for personal injury, gross negligence or fraud, or for a breach of an essential obligation, nor any right that the law grants consumers and that a contract cannot set aside.
The publisher may change these terms for one of these reasons only: a change in the law or in case law, the decision of an authority, a change in the app stores’ rules, or a new feature of the game.
A new version is shown to you in the game before it applies, with a summary of its changes.

A significant change applies only once you have accepted it, in the same way as at the first launch. Continuing to play does not count as acceptance. Until then, your campaign stays on your device, but the game can no longer be used. A minor correction, which changes neither your rights nor your obligations, does not require a new acceptance.
The previous versions of these terms can still be read on the publisher’s site.
These terms apply as long as the game is installed on your device. You may end them at any time by uninstalling the game, which erases all its data from your device.

These terms are governed by Swiss law. If you accept them as a consumer living in another country, this choice does not deprive you of the protection of the mandatory provisions of the law of your country of residence: in France, for example, those of the Code de la consommation.

If you act as a consumer, you may bring a case before the courts of Geneva (Switzerland) or those of your place of residence, and the publisher may bring a case against you only before the latter. In other cases, the courts of Geneva have jurisdiction.
No consumer mediator has been appointed to date. These terms do not deprive you of any right to go to court.
If a clause of these terms is held void or unenforceable, the others remain in force. Where the French and the English versions differ, the French version prevails.

If you obtained the game from the App Store, Apple’s standard licence agreement for apps (Licensed Application End User License Agreement) applies in addition to these terms. Where the two conflict, the provision more favourable to you prevails.
If you obtained the game from Google Play, these terms apply alone.

meta.description: Moi Président sends no data to the publisher: everything stays on your device, and deleting the app erases it all.

paragraphs.text: The game sends no data to the publisher. Everything it keeps stays on your device, and deleting the app erases it all. The publisher only receives what you write to it.
The game Moi Président is published by Matthieu Compérat, a sole trader (sole proprietorship) trading as Cosmic Studio, based in Chêne-Bougeries (Switzerland); email: support@gocosmic.dev.

nothingSent.title: Nothing is sent to the publisher

paragraphs.text: The game works offline, and no server of the publisher hosts it. It has no account, no advertising, no audience measurement and no crash reporting. It sends the publisher no data about you.
As for any app, Apple and Google may pass on to the publisher overall statistics and crash reports, depending on the settings of your device and your account.

If you write to support@gocosmic.dev, the publisher receives your email address and your message. It processes them to answer you and follow up your request, on the basis of its legitimate interest in answering the people who write to it. The exchanges are kept for as long as needed to handle your request and follow it up, then archived or deleted according to legal, accounting or litigation obligations.

They are received by Gandi SAS (France), then forwarded to a Google Gmail account; Google may process them in the United States and in the other countries where it has facilities. Google LLC is certified under the EU-U.S. and Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Frameworks, which the European Union and Switzerland recognise as providing adequate protection for certified companies.

The game stores on your device, and nowhere else: the name you choose, your campaign in progress, the history of your past campaigns, your progress and your decorations, your favourites in the Dossiers, your settings (language, theme, title of the game, the team’s note), the screens already seen and your acceptance of the terms of use (its version and date). The campaign kit, if you install it, is stored there too.
The game asks the system to leave its data out of backups (iCloud, Google account) and out of transfers from one device to another. Your game is therefore not meant to follow you to a new phone.
Delete the app: all the game’s data are erased with it.

The campaign kit is optional: its illustrations and the figures of the Dossiers. The game goes online for it only, and only when you ask: when you agree to download it, when you download or update it from its page or the Dossiers, and when you look for an update there.

Its files come from GitHub, a service of GitHub, Inc. (United States). Like any server, GitHub then receives your device’s IP address. The game sends no account, identifier or cookie. GitHub publishes no retention period for these data: its privacy statement describes what it does with them.

The links to sources and the other links to a site open that site in your browser. The site then receives what any site you visit receives, and its own privacy policy applies. The support address opens in your mail app.
The game asks you for no permission: not the camera, your photos, your location, your contacts or notifications.

website.title: The web page of this policy

paragraphs.text: This policy is also published on gocosmic.dev, the publisher’s site, separate from the game and hosted by Vercel Inc. (United States). Like any host, Vercel processes technical data of the visits, including the IP address, for its hosting logs. The site’s privacy policy describes these logs and its audience measurement, loaded only with your consent.
If a future feature were to transmit data, this policy would be updated and brought to your attention before it goes live.

The publisher holds nothing about you but the emails you sent it. You may ask for access to these data, their correction, their erasure or the restriction of their processing, object to it or ask for their portability, where these rights apply, by writing to support@gocosmic.dev. Everything else is on your device: you keep it or erase it yourself.

For any question, write to support@gocosmic.dev. You may also refer the matter to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC, Switzerland), or to the data protection authority of your country of residence (in France, the CNIL).

meta.title: About the game Moi Président | Cosmic Studio
meta.description: What the game Moi Président is and is not, its fictional figures, the notice of its simulation, its sources and its credits.

about.title: About the game
about.intro: What the game is and is not, where its figures come from, and the credits of its fonts and libraries.

paragraphs.text: Moi Président is a humorous and parodic work of fiction, loosely inspired by political news. The opponents, the parties, the events, the dialogues and the slogans are the publisher’s creations; the names of the opponents and the parties are deliberately twisted. The game reports no real fact, statement or position of any existing person, and expresses no opinion of the publisher on a person, a party or a vote.

The game gives no voting instruction. It is not affiliated with any governmental organisation, political party or activist association. It has no link with any candidate, movement, media outlet or polling institute, and is neither endorsed nor funded by any of them.

paragraphs.lead: A simplified model, with its own biases.
paragraphs.text: The game reduces political life to nine families, five axes and a few categories of voters. The opponents’ positions are estimates by the game’s team. The effects of actions, events and measures are game rules, not forecasts: they reflect design choices that others would have made differently. The game is not a source of electoral information: do not base a vote on its figures.

The game’s press review sometimes covers tragedies: disasters, riots, violence, attacks. They are rare and all fictional, inspired by real debates without their names or places: no victim is named or described, and nothing rewards taking advantage of them. The game shows no image of a real tragedy: the illustrations of the campaign kit depict fictional events and avoid violent or offensive images.

The scores, rankings, “polls”, trends and results shown in the game come from a simulation. It starts from real polls (see “Notice of the simulation”) and transforms them in every game: its figures measure nobody’s opinion and predict neither the voting intentions nor the result of the real election. French law no. 77-808 of 19 July 1977 treats a vote simulation made from polls as a poll: its notice can be consulted at the Commission des sondages.

paragraphs.lead: The die, the mark of the game’s figures.
paragraphs.text: The icon of a die, a square with dots, goes with the data, figures and values the game simulates, even without the word “fictional”: they must not be taken for reality.
Screenshots of the game must not be presented as real polls or real results.

notice.title: Notice of the simulation

paragraphs.text: In the campaign’s game space, the app provides fictional data: any figure that cites no source is a game figure, and it is fictional.

Simulation made and commissioned by Matthieu Compérat (Cosmic Studio), from 5 polls of first-round voting intentions for the 2027 presidential election, carried out by OpinionWay, Elabe, Ifop-Fiducial and YouGov, whose fieldwork ended between 10 and 22 November 2026. The page “The polls of the simulation” lists them, with their sponsors, dates and samples. The game transforms them in every game, and its figures are fictional.
Every poll has margins of error. The margins shown in the game are a game rule.
Anyone can consult the notice of this simulation at the Commission des sondages. Data frozen in version 0.2.5 of the game.

notice.frozen: Data frozen in version {version} of the game.

paragraphs.text: The starting voting intentions come from polls published in November 2026, then the simulation transforms them. They are not updated during the game and may have changed a lot since. For up-to-date figures, see the notices published by the Commission des sondages: each one names the institute that carried out the poll.

Publisher: Matthieu Compérat, trading as Cosmic Studio
The kit repository (github.com/Mitchnsun/kit-de-campagne) and its Releases carry the two parts of the kit and the prompts of its illustrations, under different terms. sections.title: 1. Briefing data (part "briefings")
body: Each figure keeps the licence of its source. The file of each indicator names the producer, the publication, the licence and the date of each source.

items: Most French public sources (Insee, ministries, IGN for the ADMIN EXPRESS COG CARTO map) are under the Open Licence 2.0 (Etalab). Any reuse mentions the source and the date of its last update.

Eurostat data may be reused, commercially too, provided the source is acknowledged ("Source: Eurostat") and any changes are indicated. Data that Eurostat attributes to another source may not be reused commercially. https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice

UNHCR datasets (Refugee Data Finder) are under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0), with UNHCR's terms of use for datasets: any reuse credits "UNHCR Refugee Population Statistics Database", indicates any changes and links to these terms; it does not suggest that UNHCR takes part in, supports or endorses the game, and uses neither its name nor its emblem as a mark. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ https://www.unhcr.org/what-we-do/reports-and-publications/data-and-statistics/terms-use-datasets
Figures from other producers (CITEPA, polling institutes…) are quoted with their source; no file from these producers is redistributed.

body: The selection, the layout and the "Good to know" notes written by the publisher are released under the Open Licence 2.0: https://www.etalab.gouv.fr/wp-content/uploads/2018/11/open-licence.pdf
Requested attribution, in addition to the source of each figure: "Moi Président, campaign kit, <month> <year> edition".
The data are dated extracts, provided with no warranty of accuracy or of being up to date. Their producers neither prepared nor endorsed this kit.

sections.title: 2. Illustrations (part "illustrations")
body: The illustrations are AI-generated; the manifest of each edition names the tool used. This part also covers the images of the illustrations/ folder. They are published to be shown in the game Moi Président. The kit repository (github.com/Mitchnsun/kit-de-campagne) grants no licence to reuse them.
The scenes and characters are fictional. Any resemblance to a real person is unintended.

sections.title: 3. Prompts (folder prompts/)
body: The texts of the prompts/ folder, the prompt template and the generation sheets of the images, are written by the publisher and released under the Open Licence 2.0: https://www.etalab.gouv.fr/wp-content/uploads/2018/11/open-licence.pdf
